nist-sp800-sec.shape_risk: sp800-53r5 is 328 near-identically structured OSCAL renders (324 controls + 4 baselines) over 20 families sharing one 4-line id/title/family/class header: 'Statement:' appears in 301/328, 'Guidance:' in 300/328, 'Parameters:' in 259/328, the case-insensitive 'the organization' statement scaffolding in 147/328, and the boilerplate citation string '(National Institute of Standards and Technology, Gaithersburg, MD)' in 218/328 — lexical hits concentrate in undifferentiated scaffolding rather than content. The same rule text is re-rendered across trees: sp800-171r3/3.5.12 ('Change default authenticators at first use') is a one-word-different twin of sp800-53r5/IA-5 ('Changing default authenticators prior to first use'), and both carry the same 'easily discoverable, and present a significant risk' guidance differing only by a hyphen ('well known' vs 'well-known'), with a third factory-default mention in sp800-53r5/SA-4.txt. The prose dirs (sp800-63, 92 .md files with distinct section titles and 41 FAQ files keyed by question frontmatter; median 2,026 B vs 3,554 B for the OSCAL controls) carry far more distinctive shapes, so mis-retrieval risk sits almost entirely in the OSCAL trees (53r5/171r3/172r3), which is why the hard query targets a 53r5 control whose span has near-duplicates in two other files.

queries.q: How short can a password be if we let the user pick it themselves?
queries.expect: Memorized secrets SHALL be at least 8 characters in length if chosen by the subscriber

queries.q: Can we let people recover their account by answering security questions?
queries.expect: Response to sets of knowledge-based questions is a form of knowledge-based authentication (KBA), and is not allowed

queries.q: Do we have to change the passwords vendors ship on new equipment before we start using it?
queries.expect: Changing default authenticators prior to first use

queries.q: What do we have to put on a flash drive that holds CUI so people know how to treat it?
queries.expect: Mark system media that contain CUI to indicate distribution limitations, handling caveats, and applicable CUI markings.

queries.q: How often should we go back and check whether our software security requirements are still current?
queries.expect: Review and update security requirements at least annually, or sooner if there are new requirements from internal or external sources
